items.title: the `Creating session...` placeholder is never removed, so it stays above the first turn and can receive an orphan delta
items.notes: Found in c13's lane report (2026-11-25): Ui.appendMsg(buf, 0, 'Creating session...') at ext/code/code.mjs:1488 is only cleared by Ui.clearMsgs from the revert path (code.mjs:1624). A normal turn leaves the placeholder in the transcript, and a part-id-0 delta used to be appended into it. Red test `placeholder :: the creating-session message is removed when the first turn starts` (assert no .code-msg element with that text after the turn). Round 64: lane a2 tip 2f97b214.

items.title: text and reasoning deltas take their part id from state, so after a dropped started event they are attributed to part 0
items.notes: Found in c13's lane report (2026-11-25): session.text.delta uses partID: state.textID, but session.text.ended derives data.assistantMessageID + ':text:' + data.ordinal; a reconnect that dropped session.text.started leaves state.textID 0 (session.step.started resets it), so the delta can never be attributed. session.reasoning.delta has the same gap with state.thinkID (line 172 vs 179). Fix: derive both delta ids the way the ended case does. c13 stopped the misdraw but this is the root cause. Red test `reconnect :: a delta after a dropped started keeps its part id` in test/code-events.mjs, plus an e2e assertion that the delta streams into the same message.

items.title: Mode.remove deletes with the raw key while the map is keyed lowercased, so a mixed-case mode survives its own removal
items.notes: Found by the core hunt 2026-11-25 at b3560073. Mode.add lowercases the key before `modes.set` (js/mode.mjs:82, 92) and Mode.get lowercases before `modes.get` (js/mode.mjs:181), but Mode.remove does `m = get(key)` and then `modes.delete(key)` with the raw argument (js/mode.mjs:165-175), so the delete never matches for a name that is not already lowercase. Every Mode.remove caller passes a capitalised name (`Mode.remove('Rich')`, `Mode.remove('Clock')`, `Mode.remove('Search Lines')`, ... in ext/*), so an extension that unloads a mode leaves it registered: its `em` and `cmds` stay reachable from Em/Cmd and a later Mode.add of the same key finds the stale mode. Red tests `Mode.remove :: drops a mode registered with a mixed-case key` and `Mode.remove :: removes the toggle command for a mixed-case key`. Failure: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: remove dropped the mode` / `+ actual { assist: {}, context: undefined, decorators: undefined, ... } - expected undefined`. The toggle command IS removed (Cmd.remove lowercases through canon), so only the map entry leaks. Fix: `modes.delete(m.key)` (or lowercase once at the top). Patch: /home/matt/worktrees/3813a9bf-ea93-4a92-8378-3ceab7116706/bred-loop/hunt-core1.patch

items.title: Em.seq never looks at buf.minors, so a command bound only in a minor mode is reported unbound and the context menu shows no key
items.notes: Found by the core hunt 2026-11-25 at b3560073. doc/Em.md gives the active stack as `[ targetEm?, minor1.em, ..., mode.em, parents..., root ]` and Em.mainGetActive builds exactly that (js/Em.mjs:145-172), but Em.seq's mode path is seqMode (js/Em.mjs:442-464), which walks `mode.em`, then `parentsForEm`, then root and never touches `buf.minors`. A command bound in a minor mode therefore resolves when pressed (look() sees the minor em first) but Em.seq returns 0. That is user visible: js/win.mjs:27 and js/menu.mjs:40 render `Em.seq(cmd, buf) || ''` as the key hint while using Cmd.get(cmd, buf) to decide the entry is enabled, so a minor-mode command shows enabled with a blank key (View mode's `scroll down` on ' ', Code Prompt's commands, man's minor keys, ...). Red tests `Em.seq :: finds a command bound only in a minor mode` and `Em.seq :: still finds the major mode binding beside a minor one`. Failure: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal: 0 !== 'C-c z'` (and `0 !== 'C-c n'`), i.e. seqA found nothing instead of the key. Fix: have seqMode search `buf.minors` in the same last-added-first order mainGetActive uses, before mode.em. Patch: /home/matt/worktrees/3813a9bf-ea93-4a92-8378-3ceab7116706/bred-loop/hunt-core1.patch NOTE for the scheduler: p141 also owns js/Em.mjs (the seq reduce), so pick takes one of the two per round; different regions, a rebase is enough.

items.title: Em.seq's answer for a space binding is '' and for 'C- ' is 'C-': it joins keys with a trailing space and then trims
items.notes: Found by the core hunt 2026-11-25 at b3560073. Em.seq reduces the key path with `acc + cur + ' '` for every key except the modifier names and ends with `.trim()` (js/Em.mjs:465-486), so the space key contributes a space that the trim then eats: a binding on ' ' decodes to '' and 'C- ' to 'C-'. Neither parses back through lib/ev-parser.mjs to the key that was bound, and the answer is what js/win.mjs:27 and js/menu.mjs:40 print as the context-menu / menu-bar key hint, so six modules' `Em.on(' ', 'scroll down')` (js/vc.mjs x10, js/shell.mjs:718, js/apt.mjs:162, js/man.mjs via View mode, js/view-mode.mjs:20) show as an empty key. Tests assert the round trip `EvParser.parse(Em.seq(cmd, buf)).join('|')` so a fix cannot just special-case the display. Red tests `Em.seq :: its answer for a space binding parses back to the space key` and `Em.seq :: its answer for a control space binding parses back to C- space`; the two plain-key tests in the file are green at base and must stay green. Failure: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal: '' !== ' '` and `'C-' !== 'C- '`. Fix: join the keys with a separator that a space key cannot produce, or trim only the final separator. Patch: /home/matt/worktrees/3813a9bf-ea93-4a92-8378-3ceab7116706/bred-loop/hunt-core1.patch NOTE for the scheduler: p140 also owns js/Em.mjs, so the two overlap and pick will take one per round; their regions are different (seqMode vs the seq reduce), so a rebase is enough.

items.title: Cmd.get picks the first minor mode but Cmd.getAll and the Em stack put the last added minor first, so the key shown and the command run disagree
items.notes: Found by the core hunt 2026-11-25 at b3560073. Em.mainGetActive pushes minors in reverse (js/Em.mjs:151-153) so the most recently added minor wins a key it shares with an older one, and Cmd.getAll prepends each minor in turn so the last added minor's command is listed first (js/cmd.mjs:124-126). Cmd.get instead walks `buf.minors` from index 0 upward and returns the first name match (js/cmd.mjs:94-98), i.e. the OLDER minor's command. With two minors defining the same command name the command that runs is not the entry listed first, and the key hint Cmd/Em report does not describe the handler. Red test `Cmd.get :: picks the same minor mode command that Cmd.getAll lists first`; it asserts the stack order and Cmd.getAll's order first (both pass at base) and then that Cmd.get returns the same handler. Failure: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: and the one Cmd.get must return` / `'a' !== 'b'`. No current mode pair happens to collide, so nothing user visible breaks today; the fix is to walk minors last-added-first in Cmd.get (and make Cmd.getAll's comment match). Patch: /home/matt/worktrees/3813a9bf-ea93-4a92-8378-3ceab7116706/bred-loop/hunt-core1.patch

items.title: a map's otherwise is skipped for any ctrl or alt key, contradicting doc/Em.md's lookup step 4
items.notes: Found by the core hunt 2026-11-25 at b3560073. doc/Em.md states the lookup as `4. If no match, try otherwise. 5. If still no match, return failure`, but look1 returns 0 straight out of the ctrl branch and the alt branch when there is no Control/Alt submap (js/em.mjs:56-83), before it ever reaches `kb = kb || otherwise` (js/em.mjs:92). So an otherwise fallback never applies to a modified key. js/ed.mjs:769-777 works around exactly this by building empty Control and Alt submaps whose own otherwise is 'close qr and pass through', which is the shape a fix should make unnecessary. Red tests `otherwise :: covers a control key with no control map` and `otherwise :: covers an alt key with no alt map`; the plain-key and no-such-key-in-a-submap tests in the file are green at base. Failure: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal: + actual undefined - expected 'fallback'`. Patch: /home/matt/worktrees/3813a9bf-ea93-4a92-8378-3ceab7116706/bred-loop/hunt-core1.patch

items.title: Pane.holdingView returns the frame's current pane instead of the pane that shows the view
items.notes: Found by the core hunt 2026-11-25 at b3560073. Pane.holdingView is `Frame.find(frame => frame.panes.find(p => p.view == view))?.pane` (js/Pane.mjs:103-106). Frame.find returns the FRAME whose panes contain the view, and `.pane` on a frame is `Pane.current(f)` (js/frame.mjs:247), the focused pane -- so with two panes in one frame the answer for a background pane's view is the focused pane. Callers use it to aim work at the pane that owns the view: ext/core/lint.mjs:132 puts the lint marker on it and ext/code/code.mjs:2182 opens the code prompt in it, so in a split frame the marker/prompt lands on the wrong pane (the one the user is not looking at). Red test `holdingView :: returns the pane that shows the view, not the frame current`, using the pane-helpers frame with two panes and pA focused; `holdingView :: a view no pane holds gives nothing` is green at base. Failure: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: the pane holding the view / false !== true`. Fix: return the pane matched by the inner find, e.g. find the pane across frames and return it rather than the frame's current pane. Patch: /home/matt/worktrees/3813a9bf-ea93-4a92-8378-3ceab7116706/bred-loop/hunt-core1.patch

items.title: batch: the man tail's escapes, spans and cells (b7: p79 p83 p34, b6: p102 p76 p77)
items.notes: Round 65's a1 lane carried two batches in sequence on one branch (b7 at 57a7e95b, then b6 at cab7cc0b), so the round takes them as one row owning the union and b6's proof. b7 absorbed p79 (a vertical table span puts its text on the bottom row: tbl(1)'s `l ld`/`r ^` example prints `|   r | foo    |`), p83 (21 groff_char(7) names: md, c*, r!, OK, Eu, sq, lf/rf/lc/rc, ul/uc/ur/ll/lr/cl/cr, 18/38/58/78) and p34 (`\v(` has no paren form: groff warns and prints `x a2b y`). b6 absorbed p102 (an unknown escape prints its own letter; groff ignores exactly 27 printable characters and warns `escape character ignored before 'Q'`), p76 (`.SY`/`.OP` keep their space in mdoc mode; groff -mdoc has no SY/OP at all, so man(7)'s layout is the reference) and p77 (a literal tab is a tab stop, `\t` is zero width in both fill and no-fill mode). items.title: batch: a delta's part id comes from the event, and a thinking block is drawn in every box (c14, c9)
items.notes: Round 65's a2 lane carried two items in sequence on one branch (c14 at 4da84e18, then c9), so the round takes them as one row owning the union. c14: `session.text.delta`/`session.reasoning.delta` took their part id from `state.textID`/`state.thinkID`, which `session.step.started` resets, so a reconnect that dropped the started event attributed every delta to part 0; both now derive the id from `data.assistantMessageID + ':text:'|':reason:' + data.ordinal`, as the ended cases already did, and the dead state is gone (the ordinal is on the event per the vendored types and live.jsonl:4). c9: `handlePartDelta` asked one view whether a delta is thinking text and returned before the per-box draw, so a second box never got the block; the reference client renders every part in every view.

items.title: js/man-roff.mjs still classifies the 27 escapes groff ignores as unknown and fails the static scan, so the inventory disagrees with the interpreter after b6
items.notes: Found by b6's lane 2026-11-25 at cab7cc0b: the interpreter now prints an unknown escape's own letter (p102), and groff ignores exactly 27 printable characters (`123456789;<=>@GIJKPQTUWijqy`, verified character by character). `Roff.scan('a \\Q b')` still returns `fails: [{ kind: 'escape', name: 'Q', cls: 'unknown' }]` and test/man-roff.mjs:165 asserts `a\\qb` fails, so the static inventory refuses what the interpreter accepts. doc/Man.md is explicit that the inventory and the interpreter must stay in sync. Fix: classify the 27 as ignored in man-roff.mjs, flip the test, and assert both halves agree for every printable character. Needs the red test written before dispatch, so next.

items.title: a literal tab in filled text is not modelled: groff advances to the next tab stop per line, b6 pinned only the .nf form and the zero-width \t
items.notes: Found by b6's lane 2026-11-25 at cab7cc0b while fixing p77. b6 separated the two mappings (a literal tab is a tab stop, the `\t` escape is zero width in both fill and no-fill mode) but only pinned `.nf` for the literal tab: `ABCDEFG<TAB>Y` is `ABCDEFG   Y` in groff (stops every 8 columns from the line's output position), and the filled case is unimplemented, so a fix that turned a literal tab into one space would still pass b6's tests. No corpus page was found to need it. Needs a red filled-mode test before dispatch, so next.
